title: Market Signal Ops Sprint Kit — Model Availability & Competitive Decomposition
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a lightweight, repeatable sprint kit for field ops that converts raw market signals (availability, latency, price volatility) into operational triggers: candidate fallbacks, procurement alerts, and engineering playbooks for rapid model substitution.
background: We increasingly rely on a mix of hosted and dedicated models. Sudden availability or pricing changes from third-party providers cause reactive firefighting. The goal is a pragmatic ops bundle product teams can run in 1-2 sprints to evaluate competitor instability and produce a prioritized fallback catalog tailored to Redwood deployment modes.
scope: Deliverables: (1) a reproducible test harness that simulates customer workloads against competitor public endpoints, (2) a signal normalization spec and scoring rubric, (3) a mapping table from signal states to Redwood actions (fallback variant, quantization recommendation, route policy), and (4) a one-page runbook and dashboard template for on-call and sales engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic workload runner can run 10 representative workloads (chat, short-generation, embeddings, rerank) against 3 public model endpoints and produce latency + success-rate histograms
Signal normalization spec is published in Confluence and includes transformation rules for missing-data and region-specific sampling
Action mapping table demonstrates at least 3 tested fallback scenarios with end-to-end validation in a staging environment
Dashboard template (Grafana/Looker) ingest sample telemetry and renders alertable metrics: availability_score, latency_tail_p95, price_change_pct
Runbook validated in a lightning exercise with SRE and a solutions engineer resulting in <30 minute run-to-fallback time in staging
tasks: Audit existing telemetry feeds for competitor model endpoints (billing logs, synthetic probes) — owner: PM
Design synthetic workload corpus and sampling cadence — owner: Research
Implement probe runner (python harness + k8s job) with retry/backoff and KV cache simulation — owner: Eng
Define signal normalization transformations and scoring weights — owner: PM + Data
Create action mapping table linking signal states to Redwood actions (fallback, quantize, route) — owner: PM + Runtime
Build dashboard template and alert rules in Grafana — owner: Observability
Run a 2-hour blast test simulating availability degradation; measure fallback time and identify cross-team blockers — owner: SRE
Produce a 1-page runbook, checklist, and postmortem template for future incidents — owner: PM
notes: 2026-03-06: Kickoff — aligned on minimum viable probe: chat short-gen (<=256 tokens), embeddings (batch size 16), and a 3-region sweep (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast).
2026-03-08: Decision to prioritize public endpoints with stable rate limits to avoid vendor TOS violations — Eng to throttle probes (10 qps max).

2026-03-10: Trade-off discussion: sampling cadence. Team prefers 15-min probes for high-sensitivity detection; finance flagged potential cost implications — compromise: 15-min for critical models, 60-min for long-tail.
2026-03-12: Eng PR opened for probe harness: github.com/redwood-inference/probe-harness/pull/42 (initial runner + k8s job spec).
2026-03-13: Data clarified scoring weights: availability 40%, latency tail 30%, error-rate 20%, price-change 10%. Will iterate after field validation.
2026-03-14: Ran baseline sweep — competitor-A had 2 regional spikes in p95 latency > 2x baseline; will run fallback scenario test on 2026-03-18.
2026-03-15: SRE requested a playbook stub for safe automated fallbacks (circuit-breaker thresholds) before any automated switch — added to tasks.
2026-03-16: Ready for first cross-functional run: Eng + SRE + Solutions on 2026-03-18 to validate the end-to-end fallback in staging.
decisions: Use weighted scoring (availability + latency tail + error-rate + price) to reduce noisy churn from transient spikes
Throttle public probes to 10 qps per endpoint to respect provider limits and avoid rate-limiting artifacts
Start with semi-automated fallbacks (human-in-loop) until we validate safe circuit-breaker thresholds in staging
risks_mitigation: Risk: Probes may be blocked or produce misleading results due to vendor throttling — Mitigation: vary probe IPs, respect rate limits, and annotate results with HTTP 429 handling
Risk: False positives triggered by transient network flakiness — Mitigation: require two consecutive probe windows (15-min cadence) before escalating
Risk: Cost of synthetic probes at scale — Mitigation: tiered cadence (critical models 15-min, others 60-min), and use sampling in non-peak hours
